category_title: Elementary student with ASD engaging in head-banging and arm-biting during transitions
student_description: Jake is an elementary student with ASD and an intellectual impairment who engages in severe, automatically reinforced self-injurious behavior (head-banging, arm-biting) when unoccupied or transitioning. Because his behavior is sensory-seeking rather than socially mediated, he uniquely requires continuous access to competing sensory input and cannot simply be ignored or left alone.

criteria.rationale: Jake's SIB is automatically maintained by sensory stimulation, so he requires alternative sensory input to compete with the urge to self-injure during downtime.
criteria.check: The tutor provides or prompts the use of a competing sensory item (e.g., textured ball) or engaging play activity during transitions or unstructured time.

criteria.rationale: Reinforcing safe, alternative behaviors helps Jake build a repertoire of non-injurious actions during independent work and transitions.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly offers behavior-specific praise or access to preferred items when Jake engages in any safe, non-SIB behavior.

criteria.rationale: Because Jake's SIB is not socially mediated, ignoring him or leaving him unoccupied will only escalate the self-injury.
criteria.check: The tutor avoids leaving Jake completely unoccupied or using 'ignore' strategies, ensuring he is actively directed to a sensory or play activity rather than just told to wait.
